events.text: Georgian house built on the estate.

evidence.quote: The Georgian house was built in 1802 .

events.text: South front refaced with red bricks.

evidence.quote: was refaced with red bricks c . 1815 .

events.text: Estate bought at auction by Ernest Terah Hooley for £25,000.

evidence.quote: In 1896 , the Anmer Hall estate was purchased at auction for £25,000 by the famed serial fraudster Ernest Terah Hooley

events.text: Prince Edward bought the property at cost from Hooley.

evidence.quote: Hooley agreed , allowing him to buy it at cost in 1898 .

events.text: Renovations added brick skin, entrance porch and tower to north front.

evidence.quote: Renovations c . 1900 added a brick dressed
skin to the north front , together with a projecting entrance porch and a tower towards the eastern end

events.text: Lease to the Duke and Duchess of Kent began.

evidence.quote: From 1972 to 1990 , Anmer Hall was leased to the Duke and Duchess of Kent as their country house .

events.label: heritage listing
events.text: Registered as a Grade II* listed building.

evidence.quote: The house was registered as a Grade II* listed building in 1984 but was later de-listed .

events.text: Lease to the Duke and Duchess of Kent ended.

evidence.quote: From 1972 to 1990 , Anmer Hall was leased to the Duke and Duchess of Kent as their country house .

events.text: Lease to Hugh van Cutsem ended (after the decade)

events.text: Surrounding estate became a scheduled ancient monument.

events.text: Duke and Duchess of Cambridge moved in as their main residence.

evidence.quote: The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge and their children moved into Anmer Hall in 2015 ,

events.text: Cambridges ended main residence use; kept as private country home.
